header: Date: 2027-04-06, Start: 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~46m; Attendees: Ethan Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Cara Liu (Redwood CSM) — Maya Chen (CatalystOps CTO), Luis Ramirez (Head of ML), Anika Bose (Platform Eng Lead), Tom Hines (Procurement)
auto_summary: Initial discovery focused on CatalystOps requirement to move away from a mix of OpenAI hosted calls and an internally run vLLM cluster. Key themes: eval parity for current prompts, latency and cost tradeoffs, private/VPC requirements for regulated data, and pilot proposal between Hosted vs Dedicated. Action items agreed: security pack, perf plan, pilot pricing, infra share.
transcript: 00:00:00 Ethan Moore: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Ethan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the opportunity. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here, CTO at CatalystOps. We pushed the calendar invite, thanks for doing this.
00:00:18 Luis Ramirez: Luis, Head of ML. I'm mainly focused on inference cost and parity vs our current outputs.
00:00:24 Priya Natarajan: Priya, SE. I'll dig into the perf and compatibility questions.
00:00:30 Tom Hines: Tom from procurement, i'll be looping in contracts later but wanted to listen today.
00:01:05 Ethan Moore: Cool. We tried to leave this as a discovery — understand your stack, constraints, success criteria, timeline. Can you give a brief picture of current infra?

00:01:20 Maya Chen: Sure. We have a hybrid setup. Customer-facing product calls OpenAI for most generation, internal tooling runs an on-prem vLLM cluster for cost-sensitive workloads. We're worried about vendor lock, cost spikes, and wanting consistent SLA across workloads.
00:01:50 Priya Natarajan: When you say vLLM cluster, is it the community vLLM or a managed variant? How many replicas, GPUs?

00:02:05 Luis Ramirez: It's community vLLM on 8xA10s right now, a few model variants — we also tried TGI on a staging pool. The main pain is managing multiple runtimes and model drift; outputs sometimes differ between OpenAI and our vLLM runs.
00:02:36 Ethan Moore: Got it. So parity between hosted OpenAI outputs and your vLLM outputs is a big driver. Are you evaluating moving everything to a single provider or keeping mix-and-match?

00:02:50 Maya Chen: Ideally one platform to simplify ops, but must match OpenAI quality for the customer-facing stuff. Also need private hosting option for our regulated clients in healthcare — VPC or on-prem is required for those accounts.

00:03:12 Priya Natarajan: On the private side, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem, keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we give reserved GPU pools and SLA — which sounds relevant if you need predictable throughput.
00:03:36 Anika Bose: Quick question — do you support bringing our existing model artifacts? We also have a small fine-tuned base on LLaMA derivatives and some adapter modules.

00:03:50 Priya Natarajan: Yes, we support custom model variants. For private deployments we can ingest containerized models and help with quantization. We also have guidance on mapping LLM inputs and KV cache management when moving from vLLM/TGI.

00:04:20 Luis Ramirez: The mapping guidance is important — we saw behavior differences around decoding and top-p between providers. We need an evaluation plan to measure regression on our prompt suite.

00:04:36 Ethan Moore: Totally. Our Optimize team typically helps craft an eval parity plan. We'll want your prompt test set and a couple of representative traffic profiles so we can run A/B parity tests across models and runtime configs.
00:05:00 Tom Hines: On the security side, SOC2 is a must. Also SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs for client audits. Do you have those?
00:05:12 Cara Liu: Cara here, CSM. We do have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO integrations, RBAC and comprehensive audit logs. We'll include the security pack in the follow-up email.
00:05:30 Maya Chen: Good. Also curious about data retention — we currently retain minimal telemetry but no PII, but some regulated clients require zero retention.
00:05:42 Priya Natarajan: We support configurable retention policies and can do no-store for certain routes + customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. For Private, data never leaves your VPC.

00:06:10 Luis Ramirez: Performance: our p95 latency target for interactive customer prompts is ~120-150ms with 1-2 tokens per request on average; cost per token is another axis. Can Redwood hit those latencies on Hosted vs Dedicated?

00:06:26 Priya Natarajan: It depends on model and batching. Hosted with optimized kernels can hit those numbers for smaller models; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower queueing variance. We can run a baseline using your sample traffic.
00:06:45 Ethan Moore: Also worth noting our smart routing can fall back to cheaper model variants when capacity is constrained — good for cost control but you can tie that to quality gates.
00:07:02 Anika Bose: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? Our vLLM setup does aggressive KV reuse which saves compute for long chat contexts.

00:07:14 Priya Natarajan: We have KV cache primitives and automatic prefix caching — plus suggestions for batching windows per route. We'll recommend cache policies tailored to your sequence length distribution.
00:07:36 Luis Ramirez: About quantization — we already quantize to int4 for some models to reduce footprint. How compatible are your runtimes with int4 quantized variants, and do you have fallback?

00:07:48 Priya Natarajan: We have quantization profiles and runtime paths optimized for int8 and int4. Some model combos may need slight accuracy tuning; we surface expected quality impact per profile.
00:08:10 Maya Chen: Pricing — we run a lot of embeddings and some heavy generation. Are there volume discounts or commit tiers for Dedicated?
00:08:20 Ethan Moore: Yes — Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated has reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits and predictable unit economics. We'll include sample pricing scenarios in the follow-up.
00:08:40 Tom Hines: For procurement, we need a ballpark headcount estimate for support and SLAs. Do you offer an enterprise support add-on?
00:08:50 Cara Liu: We have enterprise support tiers, faster SLAs and a designated tech contact for pilots. We'll outline options in the packet.
00:09:20 Luis Ramirez: On parity testing: we want to run our existing prompt suite against our current OpenAI outputs and a Redwood-hosted/Dedicated run. How reproducible are the outputs?

00:09:34 Priya Natarajan: Determinism varies; we can set seeds and decoding params to increase reproducibility. For production, we recommend evaluation thresholds and monitoring for drift with automatic rollback.
00:09:50 Maya Chen: Another constraint: some clients require data residency in EU. Do you have region pins?
00:09:58 Ethan Moore: Yes — Redwood has region-based routing and private control planes for EU regions; we can map your accounts to EU-hosted instances or do Private in EU.
00:10:15 Anika Bose: About model onboarding — we have a custom adapter that layers on a base model. Will Redwood help validate the adapter during the port?

00:10:26 Priya Natarajan: We can validate adapter compatibility, recommend quantization steps, and run small canary rollouts. We also support per-customer rollout policies and automatic fallback to a baseline model.
00:10:50 Luis Ramirez: What about monitoring and regressions? Our PMs want alerts if generation quality drops beyond a threshold.
00:10:58 Cara Liu: Console includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; we can wire your prompt suite into the monitoring so you get alerted on thresholds.
00:11:20 Maya Chen: Ok, good. Timeline: we're planning a phased migration — pilot in Q2, broader production by Q4 if things look solid. Is that realistic?
00:11:30 Ethan Moore: Absolutely feasible. A 2-week pilot to validate parity + a 6-8 week ramp to prod for Dedicated or Private typically lines up with that timeline.
00:11:45 Tom Hines: Contractual notes: we'd need liability language for regulated workloads and SOC2 evidence. Also, can you support customer-owned keys for encryption?
00:11:58 Cara Liu: Yes to both; we'll include the standard enterprise language and KMS integration notes in the package.
00:12:22 Luis Ramirez: Are there customers who have done a similar port from OpenAI + in-house vLLM to Redwood? Any reference architecture?

00:12:31 Ethan Moore: We have a few anonymized case studies and a reference runbook — for example a fintech customer moved to Dedicated and used canary rollouts. We'll share extracts relevant to hybrid migrations.
00:12:55 Anika Bose: Can you run a small benchmark against our vLLM-quantized vs Redwood runtime? We want to see throughput per GPU and p95 latency.
00:13:05 Priya Natarajan: Yes, we typically run benchmarks with your prompts and sample traffic. We'll coordinate env access or you can share logs and we'll run in our test harness.
00:13:28 Luis Ramirez: One small nit: our in-house tests with TGI had some tokenization differences causing misaligned prompts. How are tokenizer differences handled?

00:13:40 Priya Natarajan: Tokenization differences are common. We do tokenizer normalization and will map your tokenizer to the runtime's tokenization pipeline; sometimes slight prompt adjustments are needed.

00:14:05 Maya Chen: From a success criteria POV: parity within a small delta for customer-facing prompts, predictable cost for high-volume embedding workloads, and SOC2-compliant private hosting — that's our checklist.
00:14:20 Ethan Moore: Perfect, we will structure the pilot around those success criteria.
00:14:45 Tom Hines: Procurement question — if we pick Dedicated, what does the commitment model look like? Minimums?

00:14:54 Ethan Moore: Commit levels depend on GPU count and throughput; minimal commitments exist but we'll show scenarios: small Dedicated pool vs burstable capacity. We'll propose a pilot-first approach to avoid heavy upfront commits.
00:15:20 Luis Ramirez: Any lock-in concerns? We want the flexibility to switch models or providers later.

00:15:28 Priya Natarajan: We design for portability: model versioning, exportable configs, and policies for rollbacks. If you're using standard model artifacts, you can redeploy elsewhere with minimal changes.
00:15:55 Maya Chen: Do you have tooling to automate canary rollouts and A/B testing so product can measure impact?
00:16:03 Priya Natarajan: Yes, rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies are in the console. We can demo the console in the next session.
00:16:22 Luis Ramirez: On cost per embedding: we batch-embed large docs at night to save cost. Any batching suggestions?
00:16:30 Priya Natarajan: We provide batching/caching recommendations, and Optimize can suggest quantization and batching windows tuned to your workload.
00:16:55 Maya Chen: Are there any gotchas we should be aware of when moving from OpenAI models to open models on Redwood?

00:17:05 Ethan Moore: The common ones are prompt drift, tokenization, and decoding parameter mismatches. Also, some instruction-following behaviors differ; that's why we do eval parity and threshold-based rollouts.
00:17:30 Anika Bose: For the pilot, what environment access do you need? Can we give logs only or do you need API keys to our staging vLLM?

00:17:40 Priya Natarajan: Logs and sample prompts are a good start; for deeper perf benchmarks we typically ask for a staging API endpoint or a sanitized dataset. We'll be flexible with what you can share.
00:18:05 Luis Ramirez: Any automation to convert our current call patterns and rate limits into Redwood route configs? We have dozens of routes with different SLOs.
00:18:16 Priya Natarajan: We can help map route configs and suggest batching windows and autoscaling policies per route. Our onboarding runbook includes a route mapping template.
00:18:40 Ethan Moore: Quick pause — any red flags from CatalystOps side?
00:18:45 Maya Chen: Nothing immediate, maybe speed of integration for regulated clients, but you covered that with Private and KMS.
00:18:57 Tom Hines: For contracts, how long to finalize enterprise terms?
00:19:02 Ethan Moore: Typical timelines are 2-4 weeks for pilot legal review, longer for full enterprise deals — we'll coordinate with your legal team.
00:19:20 Luis Ramirez: One more technical: how do you handle multi-model routing for ensemble outputs? We sometimes run a reranker pipeline across two models.
00:19:32 Priya Natarajan: We support multi-model pipelines and reranking; you can pin different stages to different model variants and have deterministic orchestration in the runtime.
00:19:55 Maya Chen: That's useful. Okay, let's talk concrete next steps so we leave with momentum.

00:20:03 Ethan Moore: Agreed. Proposed next steps: send security + pricing pack, schedule tech deep-dive for week of 4/12, customer to send prompt set and infra inventory, Redwood to draft 2-week pilot plan. Sound right?
00:20:20 Maya Chen: Sounds right. We'll aim to send prompt set and sanitized logs by 4/9.
00:20:27 Tom Hines: Procurement will review pricing scenarios once received; expecting a follow-up by end of week.
00:20:40 Cara Liu: We'll get the materials out — SOC2, SAML, RBAC docs, pilot proposal, and sample Dedicated pricing scenarios. Ethan will own the email.
00:21:05 Luis Ramirez: Quick note — can the pilot include a p95 SLA target measurement and a small embedding throughput test?
00:21:14 Priya Natarajan: Yes, pilot will measure p95 and embedding throughput per your sample workload. We'll include the benchmark matrix in the perf plan.
00:21:40 Maya Chen: Ok thanks. One final question: who will be our single point of contact for the pilot?
00:21:48 Ethan Moore: I'll be primary AE; Priya will lead technical execution; Cara will coordinate contracts and support.
00:22:05 Maya Chen: Great, thank you all. We'll watch for the follow-up email and security pack.
00:22:12 Ethan Moore: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with materials by 4/8 and pencil in the deep-dive week of 4/12. We'll wrap now.
00:22:20 [call ends — remaining minutes used for informal side conversation not captured clearly by transcript]
